🖥 Iran vows to uphold legacy of nuclear scientist Fakhrizadeh on martyrdom anniversary

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics says honoring the martyred nuclear scientist Mohsen Fakhrizadeh means pursuing his vision for advancing Iran, promoting scientific progress, and enhancing national power.

The defense ministry issued a statement on November 28, marking the anniversary of the assassination of Fakhrizadeh.
​
The statement described Fakhrizadeh as a symbol of the bond between science, faith, and commitment, saying he believed the country’s progress depended on relying on domestic capabilities, nurturing young talent, and advancing the frontiers of science and technology.
​
The ministry added that Fakhrizadeh’s scientific endeavors reflected Iran’s determination to achieve scientific independence and overcome limitations.
​
It said Fakhrizadeh’s assassination by Iran’s enemies failed to halt the country’s scientific progress, instead strengthening the scientific community’s resolve to carry on his work, stressing that knowledge and ideas cannot be eliminated through assassination.
​
The ministry reaffirmed its commitment to scientific and technological advancement, supporting young talents, developing indigenous technologies, and strengthening scientific and industrial infrastructure, saying the path of knowledge, self-reliance, and scientific endeavor would continue, with Fakhrizadeh’s legacy inspiring future generations to build a strong and independent Iran.
​
For many years, the Zionist regime’s Mossad intelligence service had been after Fakhrizadeh, a figure who senior Zionist officials had described as the father of Iran’s nuclear program.
​
After a first plot to assassinate Fakhrizadeh failed in 2018, he was martyred in the second attempt on November 28, 2020, in an area to the east of Tehran by a group of Mossad agents who used technologically advanced equipment to assassinate the great Iranian scientist.
